title.en: Field query Separable xy grid axis nearest-neighbor sampling
title.zh: 可分离网格逐轴最近点采样

summary: Choose x-column and y-row independently nearest each query

capability: Choose the x column and y row independently nearest each query on a separable rectangular grid.
operation: separable planar grid, field values and query points -> sampled field values
discovery.model: Separable x/y axis nearest-neighbor selection; no interpolation.
discovery.geometry: Planar separable rectangular grid with x column and y row coordinates; queries are ordered coordinate pairs.
discovery.boundary: No out-of-support interpolation is synthesized; finite matched samples and in-support queries are required, and equivalence with geometric nearest on irregular grids is not asserted.

supported: Finite inputs satisfying the callable-specific shape, support, and boundary conditions

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Nonfinite sample coordinates, Q data or query coordinates reject the whole request with ValueError. Other conversion, indexing or arithmetic errors propagate. The implementation does not reject unsorted or outside-support queries; the caller determines physical support. Finite numeric object elements are checked without changing calculation inputs, and unsupported object arithmetic remains unsupported.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

example.description: Query a separable rectangular grid by independently selecting the nearest x column and y row.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.sampling import locs_to_vals

x, y = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.5, 1.0], [0.0, 0.5, 1.0])
values = locs_to_vals(x, y, x + 2.0 * y, [(0.5, 0.5)])
np.testing.assert_allclose(values, [1.5])

scope: The fixture stores 100*iy+ix, so the returned value is a lossless encoding of the selected cell; the assertion is on the choice, not on a floating value, and a constant response cannot satisfy the battery.
For six rational queries the chosen cell equals the exact axis-wise argmin pair computed independently from the stored axes.
An exact half-way tie resolves to the lower index and the choice flips just past the midpoint, so the tie rule is pinned by a discriminating pair rather than a single sample.
Queries outside the sampled range clamp to the end cell, and the answer order follows the query list including duplicates.

Failure matrix gives one executable assertion per rejecting channel: non-finite samples, field or queries raise ValueError, a malformed field shape propagates IndexError, and no partial result is returned.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes the separable nearest rule and its tie convention on sampled grids. It does not establish any interpolation accuracy, because the relation selects a stored sample and never interpolates, and it does not assert equivalence with the geometric scheme on non-separable input.
known_limitations: Rectangular and geometric nearest schemes are not asserted equivalent on irregular input
Physical interpretation outside caller-declared support is unqualified; nonfinite field values are rejected
cannot establish: any interpolation accuracy; the relation only selects a stored sample
